hitzeatlas.title: Heat atlas

hints.rasterText: Each cell covers a 100 × 100 m area. Finer differences within a cell are not shown.
hints.lstText: Measured surface temperature — not air temperature. Sealed surfaces such as asphalt and roofs reach far higher LST values than the perceived temperature.
hints.missingText: Uncoloured areas lie outside the Würzburg city boundary or were not captured by the Landsat sensor (e.g. due to cloud cover during the composite period).
hints.treesText: Only trees owned by the City of Würzburg are shown. Private trees on residential or company grounds are not recorded.

hitzeatlas.top5MethodikBody: The hotspots mark the five strongest heat centres in the captured city area. The displayed temperature is the average within a 200 m radius, to filter out small-scale outliers (e.g. individual metal roofs). A minimum distance of 600 m between markers prevents large heat islands from appearing multiple times in the ranking.

entsiegelung.title: Unsealing
entsiegelung.subtitle: Sealing degree · ATKIS Basis-DLM · OpenStreetMap
entsiegelung.interpretationBody: Each surface type is shown in its own colour — from roads and industry to residential and recreational areas. OSM parking lots (amber) and squares (blue) complement the ATKIS data.

vuln.kpiBereichSub: Highest HVI score in the dataset
vuln.interpBody: Cells with a high HVI combine above-average surface temperature and an elevated share of older residents. These areas are priorities for tree planting and unsealing measures.
vuln.formP1: The HVI combines surface temperature and senior share into an index from 1 (low) to 10 (high).
vuln.formP2Post: : cells with few residents get disproportionately high values when all residents happen to be over 65. The Bayesian estimator pulls small cells toward the city-wide mean rate ({{g65}}) — the sparser the population, the stronger. Above ~{{nPrior}} residents the observed value dominates.
vuln.formP3: is rank-normalised (0–1), so each temperature value is placed relative to the overall distribution across the city.

baum.startBodyPost: on the map to select areas for tree planting. Then set the number of new plantings and see the cooling and CO₂ effect.
baum.gapWarn: ⚠ Partly no ATKIS settlement/traffic area → assumed unsealed (green/open space) there.
baum.emptyBanner: Click cells on the map to start the simulation.
baum.sliderHelp: Diminishing returns: each additional planting increasingly covers already-shaded ground — the projected canopy cover grows ever more slowly.
baum.baumscheibe: "max {{n}}" applies to unsealed ground only. Additional plantings in sealed areas are possible via tree pits (not captured by the model).
baum.overlapWarn: ⚠ Overlap: ~{{pct}} of the new canopy area falls on already-shaded ground — no additional cooling there.
baum.methPlantableBody: The slider maximum is the unsealed cell area divided by 100 m²/tree (recommended spacing for 2nd-order trees, FLL guideline "Recommendations for tree plantings", part 1, 2nd ed. 2015). The actually available planting sites can be far fewer, since part of the unsealed area lies over basements, private property, or areas with utility conflicts. The displayed maximum is therefore a computational upper bound.

wasser.startBodyMid: (areas) on the map to unseal them. Then choose the new surface and see the annual infiltration.
wasser.estimateHint: Estimate (no hard cap) · hover for details
wasser.emptyBanner: Click polygons on the map to start the simulation.
wasser.greenest: Already fully infiltrating surface – no unsealing possible
wasser.sliderMaxHint: Max: {{n}} m² (Σ sealed area, literature values)
wasser.typicalHintPct: Typically realistic: ~{{n}} m² (~{{p}} % of total area)
wasser.gwNote: Approx. 15–30 % of the infiltration reaches the groundwater (LfU Bavaria, guideline for Bavaria).
wasser.gwWarn: Local soil properties, groundwater depth and building density in the catchment are not accounted for — value is for orientation only.
wasser.emptyResults: Select an area and use the slider
wasser.methFormulaNote: A = unsealed area (m²) · N = annual rainfall (0.5735 m/yr, DWD station 05705 Würzburg, climate normal period 1991–2020) · Ψ = runoff coefficient
wasser.methPsiTitle: Runoff coefficients Ψ by surface type
wasser.methSealNote: Share of the total area considered sealed (literature values). Determines the slider maximum.
wasser.methRealNote: Share of the sealed area that can realistically be unsealed in practice. Building footprints, foundations and infrastructurally necessary sealing are excluded. No hard cap — for orientation only.
